text:
jordan: Heads-up — ACME POC hit a 413 when sending long convo payloads during the demo. Gateway error: `413 Request Entity Too Large`. Full payload is ~6.2MB (base64 attachments + full turn history).

kevin: Oof. Can you paste the exact curl request + Content-Length? Also which deployment are they hitting (hosted/dedicated/private)?

jordan: Hosted sandbox. Example we used (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-xxl","input":"<very long base64...>","max_tokens":1024}'
```
Approx size after base64 blowup: 6.2MB. Gateway log shows: `upstream returned 413` and then `client: 10.0.0.5, uri: "/v1/generate"`.

tara: Quick options: compress the payload (gzip + Content-Encoding), stream/chunk the context, or stop sending full attachments — instead store attachments in S3 and send references or embeddings. For short-term POC, trimming to last N turns or precomputing retrieval embeddings is fastest. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

rachel: Note: base64 increases size ~33%. If ACME is embedding attachments inline that's the main culprit. Also some edge proxies reject gzipped JSON if not explicitly allowed. Test is needed.

kevin: If they must send full convo, two engineering paths: 1) presign + multipart upload to S3 and send refs (we can accept that in our ingest flow), or 2) enable chunked/streaming ingest on the gateway (needs infra change). For hosted customers we usually recommend presigned uploads or RAG.

deploy-bot: ops:deploy triggered — gateway-config v1.4.1 canary rolling (contains `client_max_body_size` tweak for nginx).

tara: I'll open a support ticket (S-1248) and attach a sanitized payload. Kevin — can you try repro locally with `Content-Encoding: gzip` + the same curl and see if gateway accepts it? Also try sending raw UTF-8 (no base64) to measure real size.

kevin: Will test now. Two notes:
- Example gzip curl: `gzip -c payload.json | curl -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @- https://...`
- If nginx still rejects even with larger `client_max_body_size`, we may need `proxy_request_buffering off;` for streaming to work. Can't change that for hosted instantly.

jordan: ACME said their plugin can't easily change how it sends data (legacy mobile plugin). They asked for a server-side workaround.

tara: For a server-side short-term fix we can: 1) increase gateway max body size for their tenant (if safe), 2) accept presigned uploads and adjust ingest to dereference S3. I'll scope both in the ticket and propose presigned flow as recommended path for production.

rachel: POC low-effort mitigation: 1) Send only last 3 turns + metadata, 2) extract and send embeddings for large attachments (we can provide a helper script), 3) compress text and remove unnecessary metadata.

kevin: Update after quick test: Gzip reduced payload ~70% and gateway accepted request on local env with `client_max_body_size` bumped. Hosted sandbox still rejected (config locked). Presigned flow likely the only immediate path without infra changes.

jordan: OK — I'll tell ACME presigned S3 + refs or RAG is the recommendation. Tara, add the presigned sample flow + helper script to the ticket.

tara: Done. Ticket S-1248 updated with sample presign flow, example curl for gzip, and recommended short-term trimming steps. Assigning action items: Jordan -> confirm with customer which path; Kevin -> follow up on infra feasibility for increasing tenant max; Rachel -> prepare helper script for extracting embeddings from attachments. :white_check_mark:

jordan: Thanks everyone — will update after ACME decides. :thumbsup:
